task.name: Break the final price tie on observed cost cohorts instead of declared price literals
task.story_text:
## Why

Candidate ordering already places reliability ahead of price: candidates are filtered to a tier,
ranked by recorded success and domain evidence, and price is consulted only to separate candidates
that are otherwise equal. The value consulted at that last step is a declared literal, which
reflects neither what the work actually costs nor any of the effects that dominate real spend —
cache behaviour, reasoning effort, retries, and promotional rates that expire on a date nobody
tracks.

Observed cost is a better value for that final step, and the substrate will hold it once
invocations are recorded with usage. It is only better at that step: an average taken across
unlike work is confounded, because models are not assigned at random and the expensive candidate
is frequently the one given the harder stories.

## Acceptance criteria

- Observed cost replaces the declared literal only at the final tie-break, among candidates
  already equal and admissible on tier, capability, and outcome or reliability evidence; the
  relative ordering produced by those earlier signals is unchanged.
- A cheaper candidate is never promoted past a candidate that ranked ahead of it on reliability
  evidence.
- Cost is compared only within matched cohorts of role, complexity, and reasoning effort; cohorts
  that do not match are not compared.
- A cohort below its sample floor, or lacking recency or completeness, falls back to the declared
  price seed, and the fallback is deterministic.
- Every selection that consulted observed cost records which cohort was used, how many
  observations it held, and whether the value came from observation or from the seed.
- Selection of which models perform generation work by cost tier is out of scope and unchanged;
  this affects only the ordering of candidates already admitted.

## Example

Two candidates admitted to the same tier and equal on reliability evidence, separated today by a
declared literal and afterwards by matched observation:

```
today       candidate X   declared max(in,out) = 75   → ranked second
            candidate Y   declared max(in,out) = 15   → ranked first

after       cohort: role=dev, complexity=MEDIUM, effort=high
            candidate X   observed median $2.10 over 14 runs   → ranked first
            candidate Y   observed median $2.90 over 11 runs   → ranked second

fallback    cohort holds 2 runs, below floor → both fall back to declared seeds, ordering as today
```

The reliability ordering that admitted both candidates is untouched in every case.

Depends on #2226

handoff.summary: Replaced the final declared-price dev tie-break with a cohort-aware observed-cost signal sourced from audit-ledger usage records, gated by matched role/complexity/reasoning-effort plus sample, recency, and completeness checks, while preserving all earlier reliability and admission ordering. plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Broken data flow: Step 1 says to build the cohort lookup in src/theforge/model_profiles.py by matching 'role, complexity, and reasoning effort', but model_profiles.py has no reasoning-effort dimension at all (no occurrence of reasoning_effort in the file); its cost data is avg_cost_usd folded per role/complexity bucket only (model_profiles.py:439-456, 1150). The substrate that actually carries role + complexity + reasoning_effort + cost_usd + cost_provenance per invocation is the #2205 ledger, read via entry_identity_ledger (src/theforge/coordinator/agent_identity.py:116-190) off audit records (schema v21, audit_substrate.py:1409-1428); the indexed invocation_identities table (audit_substrate.py:224-238) carries neither complexity, effort, nor cost. No plan step reads the ledger, aggregates it into cohorts, or extends profile recording with effort, so a dev following the plan literally has no source for the effort-matched cohorts two acceptance criteria require.
  Suggestion: Add an explicit observation-source step naming the real substrate: aggregate cohorts from the invocation ledger (coordinator/agent_identity.entry_identity_ledger over audit records, or a new cohort read in coordinator/audit_substrate.py keyed on ledger role/complexity/reasoning_effort/cost_usd), gating on full_ledger and cost_provenance for the completeness requirement; alternatively, if the cohort store is to live in model_profiles.py, add a step that extends profile recording with a reasoning-effort axis and names the recording call sites. Either way list the source module in the step's Files.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Ordering hazard the plan does not mention: the cohort key needs the pending selection's reasoning effort, but resolve_reasoning_effort runs inside _attach_routing_decision (assignment.py:3560-3573) — after candidate ranking and after budget downgrades — so no effort value is in scope at the tie-break site.
  Suggestion: Dev should derive the requested effort from the model-independent inputs (axis_decision('reasoning_effort', score, phase=...), assignment.py:2279-2314) at ranking time rather than reordering the decision flow; the provider-passthrough check at assignment.py:2204 is model-dependent and should not enter the cohort key.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 lists config/pricing.py and phrases the fallback as 'return declared price seed from price_tiebreak_signal_for', which reads as if that function itself changes. It has five other callers outside the plan's file list — config/profiles.py:371, config/role_derivation.py:261 and :321, config/models.py:432, coordinator/preflight.py:303 — none of which is a final assignment tie-break, and the last AC says they must be unchanged.
  Suggestion: State that price_tiebreak_signal_for keeps its current signature and behaviour as the seed, and that the cohort-aware wrapper is new and called only from the assignment tie-break path.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Keep the existing admissibility and reliability ranking intact, and replace only the final declared-price comparison with a cohort-aware cost signal. Add observed-cost lookup beside existing model profile/rate machinery, with deterministic seed fallback and provenance carried through assignment explanations.

steps.description: Add observed-cost cohort lookup and fallback policy
steps.details: Model the lookup on the existing recency/sample-gated profile machinery: match observations only by role, complexity, and reasoning effort; ignore incomplete observations without usage/cost; require configured or module-local sample floor and recency eligibility; return declared price seed from price_tiebreak_signal_for when the cohort is ineligible. Keep the fallback deterministic by preserving today's declared-price seed behavior.

steps.description: Wire cohort cost into the final assignment tie-break only
steps.details: Update the current _agents_by_tier/_rank_candidates price tie-break path so candidates remain filtered and ordered by tier, capability, outcome, and reliability exactly as today, then use the cohort cost signal only where price_tiebreak_signal_for is currently used to separate otherwise equal candidates. Do not let observed cost participate in tier admission or reliability ordering.

steps.description: Record cost provenance in assignment explainability
steps.details: Extend the existing assignment/explain payload with the cohort key used, observation count, and source value of observed or seed whenever the final tie-break consulted cost. Surface those fields in operator-facing explain/status output without moving selection policy into CLI code.

steps.description: Cover final tie-break, cohort eligibility, and provenance behavior
steps.details: Add focused tests showing observed cohort cost reverses only otherwise-equal candidates, never promotes a candidate over stronger reliability evidence, refuses cross-role/complexity/effort comparisons, falls back to declared seeds for low-sample/stale/incomplete cohorts, and emits cohort/source/count provenance.
